campaigns.title: Fake PS5 emulator campaign
reported_behavior: Windows malware delivered through lookalike GitHub repositories
environment and sandbox checks
Microsoft Defender exclusions
suspected information-stealing payload
cleanup script that removes campaign files
campaigns.validation_notes: The campaign is credibly reported, but public coverage does not identify exact repository URLs or file hashes. This record must not be used to accuse a specific repository.

campaigns.title: GodLoader hidden in fake developer projects
reported_behavior: approximately 200 repositories used to distribute a malicious archive
Godot resource pack used to run malicious GDScript
sandbox and virtual-machine checks
attempted Microsoft Defender exclusions
RedLine and XMRig payload delivery
campaigns.validation_notes: Check Point published file hashes but not a durable repository-path list. Ward can identify exact matching files without accusing unrelated Godot or GitHub projects.

campaigns.title: Fake Minecraft mods from the Stargazers Ghost Network
reported_behavior: malicious Java mods delivered through GitHub release archives
second-stage Java stealer
third-stage .NET stealer
campaigns.validation_notes: The report names repositories, filenames, and campaign hashes, but does not map an exact malicious file path and hash to each repository. Ward therefore keeps it in Coverage, not the repository malware database.

campaigns.title: Webrat disguised as exploit repositories
reported_behavior: password-protected release archives
administrator privilege escalation and Defender disablement
Webrat download and execution
campaigns.validation_notes: The report names repositories and describes a shared archive structure, but notes that the primary executable filename can vary. Ward does not present those paths as repository-specific malware records.

campaigns.title: GitVenom fake projects and payload repository
reported_behavior: malicious code hidden in fake multi-language projects
credential and cryptocurrency theft
AsyncRAT, Quasar, and clipboard hijacker delivery
campaigns.validation_notes: The report names Dipo17/battle as payload infrastructure but does not publish an exact malicious path for that repository. It remains Coverage rather than a malware database record.

campaigns.title: Yoba hidden in fake AI desktop applications
reported_behavior: DLL sideloading through signed OpenAI and Anthropic executables
scheduled-task persistence and attacker-selected payload delivery
XMRig cryptocurrency miner observed as a final payload
campaigns.validation_notes: The report maps three repositories to named release archives and identifies winmm.dll inside those archives as YobaDropper. Those three repository-specific entries are published in Ward's malware database.

campaigns.title: Password-protected MediaFire loader wave
reported_behavior: shared password-protected MediaFire archive linked by eight live GitHub repositories
ChaCha20 decryption of an appended second-stage Windows PE
LOCALAPPDATA staging under a Microsoft Windows Update lookalike path
Windows Defender policy exclusions for a path, process, and executable extension
administrator elevation before launching the decrypted payload
campaigns.validation_notes: Ward found 119 current GitHub repositories carrying password 5139237619. Eight live repositories resolve to MediaFire folder xpuwhpaw2jpbi and the exact confirmed malicious archive. Another 106 point to a different folder whose artifact was deleted before collection; those repositories remain historical leads and are not promoted to FAIL by this record. Five search matches did not expose a MediaFire folder URL.
